transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: This is Breach Point, I'm Priya Nair. Today: ransomware, who pays, and why it keeps working. My guest is incident responder Ben Kowalski.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Thanks Priya. Happy to be here, even if the topic is grim.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Take us back to the attack that woke everyone up.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Colonial Pipeline, May 2021. The company shut down the biggest fuel pipeline in the US and paid roughly $4.4 million in bitcoin to the attackers.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: And the casino one everyone talks about?

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: MGM Resorts in 2023. The attackers got in by calling the IT help desk and pretending to be an employee. No fancy zero-day needed.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: So are ransom payments still going up?

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Every single year. Ransomware payments set another all-time record in 2024, even higher than 2023.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: What does a breach actually cost a company these days?

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: The latest IBM figure is $4.88 million on average per data breach, the highest it's ever been.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: How do companies actually survive one of these?

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: One of our clients, a mid-size logistics firm, got hit last spring and was fully back online in 48 hours because they had offline backups. They didn't pay a cent.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: My view is never pay unless lives are at stake. Every payment funds the next attack.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Top three pieces of advice for the agencies and brands listening?

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Multi-factor authentication everywhere, train your help desk to verify callers, and actually test your restores.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Ben Kowalski, thank you. Stay safe out there, everyone.
